title_es: Caminen juntos alrededor de la casa
what_to_do: Invite the homeowner to walk the outside with you before you go up on the roof or ladder. Point at things as you go - gutters, downspouts, siding corners, window/door trim - don't just talk, walk and point.
say_en: Let's walk around together so you can see exactly what I'm looking at, not just hear about it after.
say_es: Caminemos juntos para que usted vea exactamente lo que estoy viendo, no solo que se lo cuente después.
legal_note: No claim promises yet - this is just looking together, not a scope or a price.

title_en: Point, then photograph, then explain - in that order
title_es: Señale, luego tome la foto, luego explique - en ese orden
what_to_do: Find the damage first and point it out to the homeowner in person (soft/bruised shingle, hail hit on a soft metal - vent, gutter, AC fin; cracked/dented siding, spun turbines). Take the photo with the homeowner watching, not off to the side alone. Say what it is in plain words right after.
say_en: See this dent right here on the vent cap? That's a hail hit - soft metal shows it clearest. I'm taking a picture so we both have it on record.
say_es: ¿Ve esta abolladura en la tapa del respiradero? Eso es un golpe de granizo - el metal blando lo muestra más claro. Voy a tomar la foto para que los dos la tengamos.
legal_note: Do not chalk-circle the roof before the adjuster's own photos (round 22 flagged this as disputed practice - some insurers read a chalked roof as tampered evidence). Photograph plainly; let the marks speak for themselves.

title_en: Show the photos back on your phone before you leave the yard
title_es: Muéstrele las fotos en su teléfono antes de irse del patio
what_to_do: Before wrapping up, sit or stand with the homeowner and flip through the photos you just took, side by side (undamaged spot vs. damaged spot helps a lot). Let them ask questions about what they're looking at.
say_en: Here's the good area, and here's the damaged one right next to it - see the difference? This is what an adjuster looks for too.
say_es: Aquí está el área en buen estado, y aquí la dañada justo al lado - ¿ve la diferencia? Esto es lo que un ajustador también busca.
legal_note: Never say 'this will get approved' or 'insurance will pay for this' - say what the photos show, not what a claim will do (44-8604 territory: nothing about the deductible either).

title_en: State the finding in one plain sentence, no hedging and no over-promising
title_es: Diga el hallazgo en una frase clara, sin rodeos y sin prometer de más
what_to_do: Summarize what you found in a single sentence the homeowner can repeat to someone else later. Tie it to what it means for the house, not for the insurance company.
say_en: What I'm seeing is real hail/wind damage on your roof and siding - the kind that gets worse if it sits, not better.
say_es: Lo que veo es daño real de granizo/viento en el techo y el revestimiento - del tipo que empeora si se deja, no mejora.
legal_note: Do not say the storm date qualifies them for a claim or that they 'have a case' - that edges toward public-adjuster territory. Describe the damage; the homeowner and their insurer decide the claim.

title_en: Give exactly one next step, with a name and a form
title_es: Dé exactamente un siguiente paso, con nombre y con un documento
what_to_do: Name the next step out loud and put a form in their hand for it (inspection-authorization only at this stage - not the final contract, not a contingency agreement, unless HMP's confirmed process says otherwise per the open backlog question). Give a day, not 'soon'.
say_en: The next step is just this inspection-authorization form so I can document everything properly - it's not a contract. Can I come back Thursday with the full write-up?
say_es: El siguiente paso es solo este formulario de autorización de inspección para documentar todo correctamente - no es un contrato. ¿Puedo regresar el jueves con el informe completo?
legal_note: If a contract IS signed at this visit (cash job, no insurance involved), the 3-day cancel notice and, if applicable, the deductible notice must be handed over and explained out loud, in English and Spanish (69-1601, 69-1604(3)) - never silently.
